key_insight: Oxygen content controls oxychloride framework connectivity, with fast Li-ion transport favored by low-dimensional frameworks that support three-dimensional migration through low-barrier, similar-energy Li sites.
engineering_relevance: Tuning the oxygen-to-chlorine ratio offers a design route to solid electrolytes with predicted room-temperature Li self-diffusivities up to approximately 10⁻⁶ cm²/s.
method: Crystal structure prediction and molecular dynamics using machine-learning interatomic potentials.
Potential-of-mean-force mapping and nudged elastic band calculations of Li migration.
Fine-grid compositional search across Nb-, Ta-, Ti-, Zr-, and Hf-based oxychlorides.
evidence_signal: Simulations find fast Li diffusion in Nb/Ta compositions at oxygen content x ≈ 0.67–1.5 and identify four stable candidates: LiNbO₀.₆₇Cl₄.₆₇, LiTaO₀.₇₅Cl₄.₅, LiNbO₁.₅Cl₃, and LiTaO₁.₅Cl₃.
watch_item: The stability and transport results are computational predictions; experimental synthesis and ionic-conductivity measurements are needed to validate practical electrolyte performance.
paper_title: How anion composition governs structural frameworks and Li-ion transport in oxychloride solid-state electrolytes
